setupSteps: Find the machine and read its labels. Look for the diagram of which way the pads move, the weight stack pin, and any limiter lever or pin. Brands differ; the machine's manual or diagram is the final word.

If it is the combined machine, set the direction first. Move the direction lever, flip the pad arms, or change the seat setting as the machine shows. Check the pad arms are fully locked in that mode before you add weight (this lever is where beginners usually go wrong; no single brand layout was found, so follow your machine).
Pick the lightest weight on the stack by moving the pin to the top plate. You will test the load later (Section 7).

Seat height. Adjust so your knees line up roughly with the machine's pivot point (the pad arms' turning point), as most guides say. Tall users may need to slide the seat back so the buttocks sit fully on the pad.
Sit all the way back. Buttocks at the back of the seat, spine against the back pad, feet resting on the foot plates or floor. Hips level, knees roughly above the ankles.

Pads. Place the pads on the outside of the thighs, just above the knees (a low pad on the knee joint can feel pinchy; pad height is adjustable on some machines). Pads should sit snug on the thighs, not squeezing. Most pad arms are fixed; if yours adjusts the starting width, set the start so your thighs are close together but not forced.

Range-of-motion limiter. Many machines have a pin, lever or knob that sets how far apart the pads start (for the abductor, how wide the thighs can open; for the adductor, how wide they start). Set it so the start position is comfortable and pain-free. For a beginner, use a narrower setting (smaller opening) and widen it over weeks only if there is no pinch in the hip or groin. No standard degree values for the limiter were found; the angles in Section 5 are estimates.
Grip. Hold the side handles lightly or rest your hands on your thighs; do not pull on the handles to help.
Back angle (glute vs TFL emphasis). See Section 5; for a first set, sit upright with your back flat against the pad.
Flip or switch the machine to adduction (or move to the separate machine) and re-set the seat so your knees are at the pivot.
Pads. Place them on the inside of the thighs, just above the knees, with legs resting against them.

Range-of-motion limiter. Set the starting width so your legs are open only as far as is comfortable. Do not use the widest setting; a wide start stretches the groin muscles under load, which is the position that often irritates the groin. Start narrow. Adductor machines have a similar pin or lever to set the starting opening.
Weight. Start with the pin on the lightest plate.

steps.part: A. Hip abduction (outer thighs and hips)
steps.title: Sit and settle
steps.action: Sit back against the pad, feet on the plates, hands on the handles or thighs.
steps.feel: Back supported, pads snug on the outer thighs.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back flat on the pad, hips level. Front: knees even, pads touching both thighs equally.

steps.part: A. Hip abduction (outer thighs and hips)
steps.title: Brace lightly
steps.action: Gently tighten your stomach, as if bracing for a light poke.
steps.visualCheck: Side: ribs stacked over hips. Front: shoulders level.

steps.part: A. Hip abduction (outer thighs and hips)
steps.title: Press the knees out
steps.action: Push your knees out against the pads, keeping your hips pressed into the seat.
steps.feel: Outer hip and upper buttock working.
steps.visualCheck: Side: hips stay on the seat, no tilt. Front: both knees move out equally.

steps.part: A. Hip abduction (outer thighs and hips)
steps.title: Pause at the end of the comfortable range
steps.action: Stop when your range of motion (or the limiter) says stop; hold briefly.
steps.feel: A firm squeeze, not a pinch in the hip.
steps.breathing: Hold the out-breath, do not strain.
steps.visualCheck: Front: knees evenly apart, pelvis level.

steps.part: A. Hip abduction (outer thighs and hips)
steps.title: Return slowly
steps.action: Let the pads close under control to the start.
steps.feel: The outer hip lengthening under tension.
steps.visualCheck: Side: the stack does not slam; weights move smoothly.

steps.part: A. Hip abduction (outer thighs and hips)
steps.title: Stop just before the plates touch
steps.action: Reach the start with the stack still hanging (a light touch of the plates is fine).
steps.breathing: Breathe in for the next rep.
steps.visualCheck: Front: knees back to the starting width, no bounce.

steps.part: A. Hip abduction (outer thighs and hips)
steps.title: Repeat for the planned reps, then move the pin or stand up slowly after the last rep (hold the handles while you rise)

steps.part: B. Hip adduction (inner thighs), paired exercise
steps.title: Sit and settle as in step A1, pads on the inner thighs

steps.part: B. Hip adduction (inner thighs), paired exercise
steps.title: Brace lightly as in A2

steps.part: B. Hip adduction (inner thighs), paired exercise
steps.title: Squeeze the knees together
steps.action: Bring your knees together, pushing the pads inward.
steps.visualCheck: Front: both knees close evenly; no rocking of the hips. Side: back stays on the pad.

steps.part: B. Hip adduction (inner thighs), paired exercise
steps.title: Pause before the pads touch
steps.action: Stop with a small gap between the pads (do not clap them together).

steps.part: B. Hip adduction (inner thighs), paired exercise
steps.title: Open slowly back to your limiter setting under control
steps.visualCheck: Side: stack moves without a jerk; no rounding forward at the end.

steps.part: B. Hip adduction (inner thighs), paired exercise
steps.title: Stop at the limiter, not beyond it. If the start feels like a groin stretch under load, narrow the limiter

steps.part: B. Hip adduction (inner thighs), paired exercise
steps.title: Repeat for the planned reps

commonMistakes.title: Too heavy, with momentum
commonMistakes.text: Too heavy, with momentum. Why: swinging the stack and lifting a hip uses momentum instead of the target muscles, and you may pinch the hip. Fix: drop the pin down and slow the tempo to 2 seconds out and 2-3 seconds back.

commonMistakes.title: Lifting one hip off the seat or rocking
commonMistakes.text: Lifting one hip off the seat or rocking. Why: shows the weight is too heavy or the pad is set wrongly (sources say raising a hip means too heavy). Fix: reduce the load, sit all the way back.

commonMistakes.title: Using the widest limiter setting
commonMistakes.text: Using the widest limiter setting. Why: loads the hip and groin at the end of range (adduction) and can pinch the front of the hip (abduction). Fix: narrower limiter, widen slowly.

commonMistakes.title: Letting the weight stack slam on the return
commonMistakes.text: Letting the weight stack slam on the return. Why: loses the controlled lowering and can jar the hip. Fix: 2-3 s return, stop just before the plates touch.

commonMistakes.title: Not locking the combined machine into the correct mode
commonMistakes.text: Not locking the combined machine into the correct mode. Why: the pad arms can move the wrong way or shift under load. Fix: set the direction lever or flip, check both arms are fixed, test with no weight.

commonMistakes.title: Pulling the handles or arching the back
commonMistakes.text: Pulling the handles or arching the back. Why: hides weak hips and stresses the back. Fix: light hands, back flat on the pad.

commonMistakes.title: Chasing "inner and outer thigh fat loss" with high reps
commonMistakes.text: Chasing "inner and outer thigh fat loss" with high reps. Why: spot reduction does not work (Section 9). Fix: use the machines for strength, and use overall activity and diet for fat loss.

commonMistakes.title: Going straight to adduction with a heavy stack
commonMistakes.text: Going straight to adduction with a heavy stack. Why: the groin muscles can strain with a stretch under load. Fix: start light, narrow limiter, build over weeks.

safetyNotes: Groin or adductor strain. A strain is a pain on the inner thigh, often with pain when squeezing the legs together. NHS Leeds and Berkshire leaflets say rest from aggravating activity first, and gentle movement and strengthening can begin after about 48 hours as pain allows; the adductor machine should not be used on an acute strain, and Motra's entry advises avoiding it with acute hip or groin injury. Return is gradual and pain-guided.

Hip joint problems, hip surgery or replacement. After a hip replacement, restrictions vary by surgical approach (posterior approach usually bans adduction past the midline and deep hip bending for about 6-12 weeks). Do not use the machines until your surgeon or physio says so.

Pelvic girdle pain or pubic symphysis pain. NHS leaflets advise avoiding wide, straddling and leg-splitting movements, especially weight-bearing, in pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain; the machines work in a seated splitting/closing pattern, so stop if pain appears in the pubic area or sacroiliac joints.
Knee, back, high blood pressure, shoulders: see the table.

conditionCautions.change: No breath-holding; breathe out on the effort; moderate loads 10-15 reps, 2-3 reps short of failure; uncontrolled BP: ask a doctor; machine-specific advice not found

conditionCautions.change: 2-3 non-consecutive resistance days per week (ADA at least 2); usual glucose checks if on insulin or sulfonylureas
conditionCautions.source: ADA position statement, Colberg et al. 2016

conditionCautions.change: After clearance or in cardiac rehab: light load, 10-15 reps, continuous breathing, no straining
conditionCautions.source: AHA resistance exercise statement (via ACC summary 2023)

conditionCautions.change: Part of 2+ days/week resistance work with aerobic activity
Check seat and pads fit; narrow limiter if thighs press the pads; pair with aerobic work; machine-specific advice not found

conditionCautions.change: Fits muscle-strengthening guidance; machine-specific advice not found

Warm up and keep reliever inhaler nearby

conditionCautions.change: Pads sit just above the knee; keep them above the joint line; light load, small range; stop if the knee twinges
Back pad gives support; stay upright, no arching; light load; stop if pain rises
